t: You're looking at 13 to 20 Alexander Square, a building in Kensington and Chelsea, in the south-west of London. It matters here as the birthplace of Diana Neave, who was born in this building in 1919. She became a Conservative Party worker, and in August 1979 she received a life peerage, taking the title Baroness Airey of Abingdon. That brought her a seat in the House of Lords as a Conservative member. She lived until 1992.
